R12 01 决策者收益准入遗漏
位置：pacegame/solve/feasible.py：payoff_for 在第 275 行进入 owned；第 397 至 415 行先跳过固定或早阶
段检查，第 416 行起仅求导；第 470 行起的 realised 准入循环与主 payoff、gross 准入没有检查这些 owned
收益。
公开 check_point 明确允许 payoff_for 为每个决策变量指定实际决策者的收益。该映射中的收益可与主
payoff 不同。当前代码仅对它求导，或在固定坐标、skip_optimality 路径直接跳过；一个未知或复数常数可
以在求导时消失，留下貌似正确的实数一阶、二阶结果。
最小反例：u 为实数 Symbol，主 payoff=-u²，候选 u=0，bounds=(-1,1)，gross=1，
payoff_for={u:1+I×10^-400-u²}。决策者收益在候选点确定非实，但报告返回 ok=True、complete=True；
stationarity=0、second order=-2 均通过。

共 20 个反例在三环境完全一致。NaN 与无穷也是已知无效收益；它们不应因固定坐标无可行方向或常数求
导为零而得到完整通过。未知 z 的值尚未确定，不能根据其导数为零推出收益已经可用。
合法控制：owned=-1-u² 及 2-u² 均正常通过，允许不同决策者拥有不同收益及有限负净收益；原主 payoff 的
1+I×10^-400 仍正确拒绝。此问题不要求收益非负。
范围：本反例限定于公开低层 check_point 的 payoff_for 入口。主 solve 仍有各玩家符号求值和已实现收益守

已知无效值是违反，未知值是 required warning 并使 complete=False。覆盖四条路径、NaN、无穷、两个虚
部尺度和合法不同收益，保留主流程守卫。

位置：analyze/verify.py 第 133 至 138、349 至 356 行；analyze/equilibrium.py 第 38 至 65、116、172 行；
analyze/statics.py 第 148 至 158 行。主 engine 第 500 至 507、543 至 551 行也先把收益转为 float。
策略和不同参数点的收益先分别转换为 binary64。只要共同基数较大，一个有明确符号的精确差额就可能在
比较前消失。最终两路线检查也把符号值转为 float，两条路线一致不证明保留差额被保存。本轮固定决策

PACEgame A Python toolkit for inspecting continuous time
entry and signalling models
Author names, affiliations, corresponding author and contact details require author confirmation before
submission.
Original Software Publication • Review revision 0.2.10 • 8 October 2026


Highlights
• Combines replaceable demand primitives with symbolic timing-model payoffs.
• Distinguishes fixed decisions, numerical corners and unresolved searches.
• Retains parameter and candidate values before search and necessary derivatives.
• Checks retained joint curvature at interior and critical boundary points.
• Provides source, wheel, offline core dependencies and reproducibility records.


Abstract
PACEgame is a Python toolkit for inspecting continuous-time entry and signalling models. It connects
replaceable demand lifecycles and share rules to symbolic payoffs, sequential numerical searches, local
diagnostics and sampled claim reports. Users can compare conditional strategy scenarios, differentiate
resolved candidate outcomes and export version-bound evidence. The package includes two demand
lifecycles, two share rules, three model factories, a command-line interface and executable examples.
Numerical states distinguish model corners, fixed decisions and exhausted computational searches.
Required checks expose missing evidence; isolated share sensitivity excludes cost-only responses. Claims
require accounted samples, and non-finite differences cannot establish signs. A supplied costless-signal
example reaches a finite payoff limit, showing why a search cap does not prove divergence. Stock, cost,
signal-bound and readiness-lag variants illustrate how assumptions change candidate rankings and
sampled propositions. Typed cache keys preserve model state, and derivative claims bind their stated
player. Retained parameters, objectives and candidate values align search and necessary derivatives.
Domain conversion exposes coordinate precision loss. Final payoff comparisons guard tested
cancellation. Structural symbols and players remain distinct. Retained endpoints, tolerance signs and
finite-real payoffs protect reported candidates. Validation includes 450 tests, independent quadrature and
analytic sequential, crossing and fixed-domain examples. General-horizon checks align entry domains,
costs and cumulative-demand bounds. The software is intended for researchers, reviewers and instructors
working with stylized timing models. Finite searches, local diagnostics and sampled claims do not certify
global optimality, continuous-domain propositions or Nash equilibrium. The delivered archive supports
review; public archival identifiers and confirmed author declarations remain pending.
Keywords: entry timing; signalling; sequential decisions; symbolic computation; numerical verification;
research software

1. Motivation and significance
Researchers studying platform entry, deployment timing and preannouncement often integrate a demand
path, differentiate its payoff and compare four policy scenarios. A stationary point does not establish a
feasible maximum. It can lie outside the horizon, represent a minimum or omit a relevant corner. A
numerical substitute creates additional questions: which points could be evaluated, whether the search
stopped at a computational budget, and whether a purported proposition was tested everywhere requested.
PACEgame addresses this inspection task with reusable model primitives and explicit result states. A user
supplies a lifecycle, a rule allocating new demand, and the ownership and order of decisions. The same
components generate payoffs, search domains, local diagnostics, parameter sweeps and sampled claim
reports. Demand assumptions can change within the same inspection procedure. The software
contribution is the connection between model specification, constrained candidate search and auditable
reporting, rather than a new theorem about entry timing.

The intended users are researchers developing stylized entry models, instructors teaching sequential

specification rather than observational data. Applications to actual adoption, industrial deployment or
policy require separate identification and calibration. No independent user adoption, empirical validation

2. Software description
2.1. Architecture and model contract
The package contains four layers (Fig. 1). Core classes define demand segments, installed stocks, demand
shares, strategies and costs. Model factories compose these primitives. The solver retains actual numerical
parameter values before substituting into symbolic payoffs and searches according to the declared move
order. Analysis modules assemble candidate rankings, finite-difference responses and claim reports.
Plotting is an optional presentation layer; all numerical operations use Python and SymPy without
importing Matplotlib [5].
A Lifecycle implements segments, stock_at and capacity. Segments store intervals and symbolic demand
integrals. TwoPhase represents constant arrivals followed by maturity; Logistic measures adoption from a
common time-zero origin. A ShareRule allocates arriving users from installed stock. Proportional uses
relative quality and a stock-dependent network term; Logit uses exponential weights. Parameters are
stylized, not empirical estimates. capacity bounds cumulative endogenous demand, excluding externally
created stock. TwoPhase uses sigma(growth_end×horizon−growth_end²/2); Logistic uses the loose bound
ceiling×horizon. A carried stock contributes at most stock×horizon to integrated demand. This diagnostic
envelope does not impose customer conservation.

2.2. Candidate search and diagnostics
The numerical path performs backward recursion over the declared stages. At each stage, an objective
evaluation includes the continuation selected by later stages. One-dimensional searches scan a grid and
refine a neighborhood; joint choices use a product grid followed by coordinate refinement. Model corners
are included. This procedure produces numerical candidates, not a global certificate: narrow peaks,
multiple separated maxima and discontinuous follower responses can defeat the finite scan. Every result
retains an explicit search-assurance warning.
For an open upper domain, a doubling probe supplies a finite search box. Exhausting that budget
produces the search-limit state. The state is unresolved: finite observations cannot distinguish a distant
finite maximum, an unattained finite supremum and an infinite payoff. The current numerical routine
does not infer unbounded payoff from such a probe. Search-limit flags from discarded follower
continuations are not accumulated into the selected continuation. Invalid or unresolved candidates cannot
participate in payoff comparisons or comparative statics, and a ranking with no valid candidate returns no
best label.
Tolerances pass retained finite-real and nonnegative-sign checks; nonzero binary64 underflow or
overflow rejects. Diagnostics validate coordinate/bounds coverage and known kind labels against actual
positions. Omitted labels are inferred. Corner classification, derivative evaluation and membership use the
same retained candidate. Membership and payoff ceilings retain the admitted tolerance. Net and supplied
gross payoffs require finite-real evidence before conversion; known invalid values fail and unknown
values prevent completion. Derivative heuristics still use numerical approximations. Checks cover
bounds, reported-payoff finiteness, independent final-value payoff agreement, supplied gross payoff and

Fixed decisions have no one-sided test. Equal declared objectives receive shared joint Hessian checks at

Parameter-retained objectives enter compiled and cancelled evaluation; symbolic fallback retains trial

decreasing its evaluated value. The share diagnostic isolates explicit share-rule sensitivity through a chain
rule, holding decisions, installed stocks, lifecycle and costs fixed. Independent stock and share
placeholders prevent a shared parameter’s cost or demand path from being mistaken for share activity. A
custom payoff or share path must declare a share_sensitivity hook; otherwise this diagnostic is unknown.
A 1e-12 absolute sensitivity tolerance distinguishes activity, numerical inactivity and unknown results. A
nonzero result establishes local activity. All-zero sensitivity falsifies that activity claim without
invalidating the payoff; unavailable sensitivity yields no verdict. None establishes the absence of
competition globally.

2.3. Claim reports and interfaces
Users express comparisons, interiority, feasibility, magnitude bounds and derivative signs as claims. Sign
accepts d pi_<player> / d <parameter>, binding either current player’s payoff. Unknown targets,
parameters, strategies and malformed expressions reject before sampling. Decision responses remain
available through derivative(quantity=<decision>), outside Sign; payoff gaps require quantity="payoff".
Claim iterables, including generators, are materialized once. Reports separately count passes, failures,
skips and computation errors, retaining parameters and reasons. Feasible cannot pass after a failed solve
or incomplete required checks. Interior concerns a whole valid candidate and skips unresolved or invalid
parents, even if a follower coordinate has an interior label. This scope does not assert a separately
conditional follower fact. A claim holds only when every requested sample receives a verdict and none
fails. Report.ok excludes errors and counterexamples; Report.complete also excludes skips and requires
each claim’s counts to equal the requested point count; an empty or partially evaluated report cannot be
complete. Finite-grid success is evidence on samples, not a regional theorem.
The Python entry point rank_strategies names the actual comparison. equilibrium remains a compatibility
alias, and output always states that it is not Nash-certified. Sweeps consume a nonempty unique admitted
strategy iterable once; empty values return an empty list after pool validation. Sweeps, verification axes
and command-line overrides reject unknown parameter names. For backward compatibility,
Game.numeric ignores inactive names in dictionaries containing alternative model switches. Users
needing strict name checks should use the documented interfaces rather than infer strictness from that
conversion helper.
Comparative statics use finite differences of resolved candidates, recording a feasible one-sided stencil
when central perturbation leaves the parameter domain. Difference denominators, numerators and final
slopes must be finite. Overflow raises a numerical-range error, recorded as a claim error without a sign
verdict; the sign accessor also rejects non-finite slopes. Kinks and regime changes need step-size checks.
Threshold routines retain sampled zeros between opposite nonzero signs and refine direct sign-change
brackets. A sampled zero run returns a representative point, not a unique transition boundary; endpoint

The baseline point uses sigma=0.1, phi=0.85 and growth_end=0.3. Silent labels DF and DL choose

4. Impact
The demonstrated benefit is a more inspectable analytical workflow. A user can connect the supplied
model, numerical candidate, local diagnostics and sampled proposition through one versioned output
record. The baseline finite-asymptote example and the deliberately broken-payoff regression establish
concrete cases where the revised reporting changes the conclusion available to a reader. The benchmark-
failure regression prevents an unsuccessful program from producing a plausible performance observation.
These are verified behaviors in the delivered release, not evidence of external uptake.
Potential reuse includes teaching entry-timing trade-offs, checking the consequences of stock and cost
assumptions, and reviewing symbolic claims against constrained numerical candidates. Switching from
TwoPhase to Logistic or from Proportional to Logit exercises the same interfaces. Asymmetric quality
can expose locally active parameters away from a boundary. Extensions retain diagnostics only when they
satisfy the documented model and parameter contracts; a custom economic specification remains the
modeller’s responsibility.
Practical reproducibility comes from the installable wheel, offline core dependency set, shipped
examples, environment records and checksums. This supports artifact review without pretending that a
locally delivered archive is a permanent public repository. Before journal submission, the authors must
supply verified identities and support contact, publish a frozen source version and permanent archive, and
confirm declarations. Those identifiers are explicitly pending in the metadata tables. Claims of citations,
download counts, course adoption or industrial use require evidence that was not supplied.
Limitations include finite heuristic searches, local diagnostics, rectangular bounds, fixed two-player roles
and uncalibrated demand. Feasibility cannot remove these limits. Full simultaneous interactions, certified
global optimization and continuous-domain proofs remain outside the release. Detailed audit evidence
accompanies the package.


5. Conclusions
PACEgame 0.2.10 provides a reusable route from continuous-time demand primitives to symbolic
payoffs, constrained numerical candidates and sampled claim reports. Explicit fixed-domain, required-
check and sensitivity states prevent distinct computations from being reported as the same outcome.
Typed cache state, consistent retained parameters, candidates and derivatives, independent structural
symbols, distinct players, retained joint interior and critical feasible curvature and accounted samples
align outputs with their meaning. Retained endpoints, tolerance signs, finite-real payoff admission and
ceiling differences prevent these audited false acceptances. Source and wheel regressions, quadrature and
